root.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: Retreat Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 Be7

overview: Black retreats the bishop to e7 after 4.Bd2, giving a solid Queen's Gambit-style position with the bishop already out. White usually plays 5.g3 with Bg2 and O-O, or e3 and Bc3-style set-ups, while Black plays ...d5, castles and prepares ...c6 or ...dxc4. The game is steady and manoeuvring, with a Catalan-like feel.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, then castle
Keep a slight space edge with Qc2, Bc3 or Nc3
Press on the c-file and the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Set up a solid centre with ...d5, ...O-O and ...c6
Challenge with ...dxc4 and ...b5 or ...c5 at the right moment
Reach a safe, equal Queen's Gambit-style structure

typical_structures.structure: Queen's Gambit Declined structure with c4/d4 against c6/d5/e6
Semi-open c-file after exchanges on c4

character.notes: Solid, low-risk set-up for Black with few ways to lose quickly.

soundness.notes: Sound and respectable for both sides.

structure.notes: Tension in the c4/d4 v d5/e6 centre; a QGD-style structure, so flexible.

approach.notes: A mainstream defence, played by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the subtle positional play against a fianchetto takes practice.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.g3 d5 line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 Be7 5. g3 d5 6. Bg2
sublines_that_differ.how: The main line, a Catalan-style set-up with Bg2 against Black's QGD shell.

character.reason: Black gets a compact, safe QGD-style position.

structure.reason: Centre in tension with c4/d4 against d5/e6.

plans.reason: White's g2 bishop on the long diagonal.
